title: 2005 AMC 10A Problem 19
statement: Three one-inch squares are placed with their bases on a line. The center square is lifted out and rotated \(45^\circ,\) as shown. Then it is centered and lowered into its original location until it touches both of the adjoining squares. How many inches is the point \(B\) from the line on which the bases of the original squares were placed?

solutions.text:
When lowered, the rotated square’s two lower edges rest on the inner top corners of the adjoining squares, which are at height \(1.\) The bottom vertex is centered between those corners, so each corner is horizontally \(\tfrac12\) unit from it. A lower edge has slope \(1\) in magnitude, so it rises \(\tfrac12\) unit on the way to a corner. Therefore the bottom vertex is at height \(1-\tfrac12=\tfrac12.\)

Point \(B\) is the opposite vertex, a full vertical diagonal of length \(\sqrt2\) higher. Its height is therefore \(\tfrac12+\sqrt2.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: After the \(45^\circ\) rotation, the square’s diagonal (length \(\sqrt{2}\)) is vertical, with \(B\) at the top vertex
Use a lower edge’s \(45^\circ\) slope and its contact with an adjoining top corner to locate the bottom vertex
